title: Stalemate tricks
line: The last resource when losing, and how not to fall for it.

steps.text: White is a queen up and threatens mate. But look at your king: it has no move. If the rook were gone, it would be stalemate.
You have Black. Check the white king with your rook, and keep checking.

wrong.g2g3: That does not check, and White soon mates.
wrong.g2g4: That does not check, and White soon mates.

steps.hint: The rook checks along the king's file.
steps.after: If the rook is taken, it is stalemate. If not, it checks again.

steps.text: Check again, right beside the king. If it takes, you have no move.

wrong.f2e2: After that check, White escapes and has a forced mate.

steps.hint: Put the rook next to the white king, with check.
steps.after: Taking the rook is stalemate. Running from it means more checks. The game is drawn.

steps.text: Now you have White, in the first position. Mate before the rook starts checking.

wrong.f7f8: That lets the rook start its checks. Taking it means stalemate, so the game is drawn.
wrong.f7f6: That lets the rook start its checks. Taking it means stalemate, so the game is drawn.

steps.hint: Check the king with the queen. If the rook blocks, take it.
steps.after: The rook can only block, and the next move is mate.

summary: When your king has no move, a piece that checks forever, or gets taken into stalemate, can save a lost game.
